bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — The Company derives a significant portion of its revenue from its ten largest customer groups; any deterioration in these relationships would adversely affect operations, financial condition, performance and cash flows. Management points to strong client stickiness, high retention and the collaborative nature of OEM engagements, and to using aerospace expertise to open adjacent precision-driven segments.
- Geographic concentration - all manufacturing clusters in Karnataka — All manufacturing cluster units are located in Karnataka, India, leaving the Company exposed to region-specific risks. Mitigation is the planned facility at the upcoming greenfield Aerospace & Defence manufacturing cluster near Hosur, Tamil Nadu, focused on aero-engine and gear box systems requiring complex, ultra-precision manufacturing, and intended to deepen participation in the global aerospace engine supply chain across forging, precision machining and specialised surface treatment for engine-grade alloys.
- Aerospace industry demand dependence — Any slowdown or decline in Aerospace demand may adversely affect business operations, financial condition, results and cash flows. The Company is diversifying into consumer durables and intends to build similar long-term OEM engagements to reduce reliance on the Aerospace segment, replicating its machining and special-process capabilities across other precision-driven sectors.
- Supply chain disruption and single-source dependence — Global and domestic disruptions - geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, logistics bottlenecks, material shortages, dependence on single-source suppliers and vendor financial instability - could affect availability, cost and timely delivery of critical inputs. Mitigated by qualifying multiple vendors (key suppliers approved by large OEM customers), alternate sourcing, periodic vendor audits, due diligence and long-term contracts.
- Export and cross-border exposure (flagged as the Key Concern in FY 2026) — A significant portion of revenue comes from customers outside India while raw materials, components and equipment are sourced from global suppliers, exposing the Company to global economic, political and regulatory change. Current geopolitical developments and regional conflicts affecting shipping, energy and logistics networks may delay receipt of raw materials and components and raise input, freight and insurance costs, hitting manufacturing schedules, cost structure and results.
- Capital investment and funding access — Operations require substantial capital expenditure for maintenance, replacement and upgradation of equipment and machinery; constraints in accessing adequate capital would adversely affect the business. Mitigated through a prudent capital structure, monitoring of key financial ratios, compliance with lender covenants, regular capital planning, cash flow management and diversified funding sources.
- Foreign exchange movements — Adverse movements between the Indian Rupee and foreign currencies may affect the value of the Company's equity shares irrespective of operating performance and financial results; mitigated through a combination of natural hedging and prudent treasury management.
- Regulatory, chemical-compliance and data-security exposure — Non-compliance with corporate, environmental, labour and safety regulations - or changes to them - may adversely affect the business, addressed through a compliance framework of periodic audits, internal controls, training and monitoring. The BRSR adds two specific structural exposures: aerospace coatings, solvents and polymers plus toy-grade PVC/ABS/PP pigments are regulated as hazardous substances requiring REACH and RoHS compliance (failure risks export restrictions and penalties), and the handling of proprietary designs and aerospace/defence-related sensitive information creates customer-IP and data-security risk addressed via an ISO 27001 ISMS, penetration testing and cybersecurity audits.

outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: Aequs signed MoUs with the Governments of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, including a Rs 1,900 crore investment at Hosur to establish an integrated aerospace ecosystem focused on aero-engine components and complex landing-gear components; the Chairman describes the Tamil Nadu MoU as an intent to invest that amount over ten years. Separately, and as a firm commitment, the Company has approved cumulative investment of Rs 2,856 crore over five years across its Belagavi and Hubballi clusters in Karnataka to expand aerospace precision engineering and consumer manufacturing capacity. Commercial production for Consumer Electronics commenced during Q3 FY26, with further investments planned for FY27 including the ongoing construction of a new facility at Hubballi to support higher production volumes and meet growing customer demand. At Hosur the immediate focus is a phased execution plan, with investment sequenced against customer requirements, identified programme opportunities and the specialised capabilities that aero-engine and landing-gear components demand - management frames it as 'no ordinary greenfield, but one built on the considerable aerospace execution knowledge already established at Belagavi'. Across Belagavi and Hubballi, investment is directed towards strengthening manufacturing capability, supporting programme scale-up and improving operational readiness; as recently commissioned capacities mature the emphasis shifts to utilization, productivity improvement and operating leverage. The Company intends to phase investment in line with customer requirements, programme visibility and capability needs, funded off a balance sheet that strengthened materially during the year together with retained IPO proceeds. Reported capacity utilization stands at 62% for Aerospace (against a stated India average of 70%) and 23% for Consumer, leaving substantial headroom in recently commissioned assets. Other capability-building steps during the year include a partnership with IIT Dharwad to establish an advanced materials R&D ecosystem, and Ajna Aerospace and Defense (established 2026) which aims to build an end-to-end Unmanned Aerial Systems ecosystem spanning integration, manufacturing, testing and commercialization.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising aircraft production rates are increasing demand across the programs in which Aequs participates
- Global OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers are seeking to simplify fragmented supply chains and work with partners capable of absorbing larger and more complex work packages - favouring Aequs' qualified portfolio, delivery record and vertically integrated ecosystem
- Aerospace programme life-cycles often extend over several decades with rigorous qualification and stringent quality standards, creating significant barriers to entry and durable revenue visibility
- Consumer Electronics fixed cost base is substantially in place while volumes are still ramping; as volumes scale, stronger fixed-cost absorption and operating leverage are expected to carry the segment towards sustainable profitability
- Reported net loss is driven by depreciation and finance costs on capacity commissioned over the last twenty-four months plus the ramping Consumer Electronics cost base - described as an investment cycle 'now behind us in spending terms and ahead of us in returns'
- Balance sheet strengthened materially during the year; together with retained IPO proceeds this gives headroom to invest without straining the capital structure
- Global aerospace industry growth driven by rising air travel, higher aircraft production, MRO expansion for ageing fleets and increased outsourcing to Tier-1/Tier-2 suppliers as OEMs focus on design and final assembly
- India offers a significant cost advantage through competitive labour costs and lower overheads versus US and European aerospace hubs; Make in India, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, PLI and favourable SEZ policies support the sector
- Indian aerospace manufacturing market projected to reach Rs 257.09 Bn ($3.06 Bn) by 2030, with the largest projected 2030 sub-segments being aerostructures, landing systems and actuation systems
- Threats flagged for the industry: dependence on imported raw materials and components exposing manufacturers to supply-chain disruption, geopolitical risk and input-cost volatility; and a mismatch between education and industry requirements limiting job-ready talent
- Consumer durables demand supported by rising domestic demand, rapid urbanization, an expanding middle class and improving product affordability; India's consumer durables/electricals/EMS sector expected to see gradual recovery
- Global EMS market projected to grow from $689.86 Bn in CY2026 to $1,192.68 Bn by CY2034 (7.10% CAGR); global toys market to reach $223.74 Bn by CY2035 (6.62% CAGR); global cookware to grow from $38.34 Bn in 2026 to $67.87 Bn by CY2034 (7.40% CAGR)
- Educational and skill-building toys gaining prominence as parents increasingly view learning-and-play products as developmental rather than discretionary
- Indian cookware demand shifting toward premium, health-conscious and induction-compatible categories (hard-anodized, tri-ply stainless steel) as incomes rise; Indian cookware market expected to reach $5.70 Bn by 2034
- Aerospace order book stood at USD 889 million as at March 31, 2026, described as robust and supporting improved revenue visibility
- Aerospace portfolio expanded to 5,654 SKUs during the year; each new part undergoes rigorous qualification and is typically tied to a long-term programme, which deepens customer relationships and improves revenue visibility

Its differentiator is an integrated 'ecosystem' model that clusters specialised manufacturing capabilities, infrastructure and partnerships on connected platforms, proven at Belagavi over fifteen years and now being extended to Hubballi and Hosur.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and single-source dependence
risks.note: Global and domestic disruptions - geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, logistics bottlenecks, material shortages, dependence on single-source suppliers and vendor financial instability - could affect availability, cost and timely delivery of critical inputs. Mitigated by qualifying multiple vendors (key suppliers approved by large OEM customers), alternate sourcing, periodic vendor audits, due diligence and long-term contracts.

risks.risk: Export and cross-border exposure (flagged as the Key Concern in FY 2026)
risks.note: A significant portion of revenue comes from customers outside India while raw materials, components and equipment are sourced from global suppliers, exposing the Company to global economic, political and regulatory change. Current geopolitical developments and regional conflicts affecting shipping, energy and logistics networks may delay receipt of raw materials and components and raise input, freight and insurance costs, hitting manufacturing schedules, cost structure and results.

Operations require substantial capital expenditure for maintenance, replacement and upgradation of equipment and machinery; constraints in accessing adequate capital would adversely affect the business. Mitigated through a prudent capital structure, monitoring of key financial ratios, compliance with lender covenants, regular capital planning, cash flow management and diversified funding sources.

Adverse movements between the Indian Rupee and foreign currencies may affect the value of the Company's equity shares irrespective of operating performance and financial results; mitigated through a combination of natural hedging and prudent treasury management.

Non-compliance with corporate, environmental, labour and safety regulations - or changes to them - may adversely affect the business, addressed through a compliance framework of periodic audits, internal controls, training and monitoring. The BRSR adds two specific structural exposures: aerospace coatings, solvents and polymers plus toy-grade PVC/ABS/PP pigments are regulated as hazardous substances requiring REACH and RoHS compliance (failure risks export restrictions and penalties), and the handling of proprietary designs and aerospace/defence-related sensitive information creates customer-IP and data-security risk addressed via an ISO 27001 ISMS, penetration testing and cybersecurity audits.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Aequs Limited manufactures precision-engineered components, forgings and aerostructure assemblies for the aerospace industry and high-value consumer products including toys, kitchen and home appliances and precision device enclosures for consumer electronics. It sells only to institutional B2B customers - global aircraft OEMs and Tier-1 system integrators, and global consumer brands - under long-term, programme-based agreements. Its differentiator is an integrated 'ecosystem' model that clusters specialised manufacturing capabilities, infrastructure and partnerships on connected platforms, proven at Belagavi over fifteen years and now being extended to Hubballi and Hosur.

one-line thesis: Aequs delivered a landmark FY26 with 33% revenue growth and a $889M aerospace order book, but consolidated PAT remains negative due to aggressive consumer electronics capex depreciation. The investment thesis hinges on achieving consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27 and sustaining 20%+ aerospace margins as new Hosur and Karnataka capacities commission.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 12,304 Cr (+33% YoY); EBITDA: INR 1,545 Cr (+43% YoY, 13% margin); PAT: Loss of INR 1,133 Cr (improved from -11% to -9% margin); Order Book: $889 Mn (Aerospace only); Net Debt/Equity: 0.23x. One-offs/Distortions: Q4 PAT loss of INR 541 Cr driven by full run-rate depreciation on new consumer capex before utilization ramped; Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% includes other income, operational margin guided at 20%.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: 45-50% consolidated (Aerospace 25-30%, Consumer 125-150%); Margins: Aerospace ~20% EBITDA, Consumer to reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27; Order Inflow: Continued addition of 100+ SKUs/quarter in Aerospace; Capex: INR 660 Cr total (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer).
order book & pipeline: $889 million in Aerospace (approx. 8-9x trailing aerospace revenue); robust visibility driven by 433 new parts added in Q4 alone (total portfolio 5,654 SKUs); long-term agreements with global OEMs for engine and landing gear components.
segment / subsidiary detail: Aerospace: Revenue INR 10,464 Cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA INR 2,813 Cr (+76% YoY), ROCE 20%. Consumer: Revenue INR 1,840 Cr (+84% YoY), EBITDA Loss INR 783 Cr (loss widened due to new capacity commissioning); utilization currently 23%, targeting 40-50% in FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: New INR 1,900 Cr MoU for vertically integrated aero-engine/landing gear park in Hosur (Tamil Nadu); INR 2,856 Cr expansion in Belagavi/Hubballi; moving up value chain into engine components (revenue impact from FY28); PLI scheme eligibility starting FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Aerospace margins sustained at ~20% operational level despite mix changes; Consumer margins depressed by low utilization (23%) and high fixed depreciation; material cost inflation (titanium/steel) passed through to customers via long-term agreements; logistics costs up slightly due to West Asia crisis but deemed non-material.
capex / expansion: FY27 planned capex INR 660 Cr (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer); FY26 saw significant asset base expansion leading to gross block of ~INR 830 Cr in Consumer; funding via borrowings and internal accruals; depreciation run-rate ~INR 45-46 Cr/quarter plus additions.
capital allocation: Prioritizing capacity expansion for confirmed customer demand (Mattel, Apple ecosystem); net debt/equity improved to 0.23x post-IPO; cash balance INR 3,015 Cr; no dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode for growth.
risks & watch-items: Consumer segment ramp-up delay beyond Q4FY27; dependency on single large consumer electronics customer; geopolitical supply chain disruptions (West Asia) impacting logistics and raw material lead times (Titanium 52 weeks, Steel 65-75 weeks); key management change (CFO stepping down); equipment sourcing constraints from China.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth and moat (vertical integration, speed-to-market); transparent about short-term P&L pain from consumer capex; pragmatic on working capital buildup due to geopolitical stocking; committed to margin recovery via utilization.
non-obvious takeaways: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% reported includes other income and excludes unallocated corporate costs; true operational margin is ~20%; Consumer electronics and Aerospace share 'precision manufacturing' platform capabilities but use distinct machine bases (CNC for metal/aero/electronics vs. Molding for plastics/toys); PLI benefits only start accruing in FY27.
